title: After Decades Without Title, Nuevo Laredo’s Tecnológico Finally Holds Deeds to Its Campus
excerpt: After decades without legal title to its own land, the Instituto Tecnológico de Nuevo Laredo now holds the deeds to more than 170,166 square meters of its campus, after the municipal government delivered the property documents on Wednesday.
content:
After decades without legal title to its own land, the Instituto Tecnológico de Nuevo Laredo now holds the deeds to more than 170,166 square meters of its campus, after the municipal government delivered the property documents on Wednesday, Nov. 18, according to Nexus Tamaulipas.

The delivery, led by Mayor Carmen Lilia Canturosas Villarreal working with the Colegio de Notarios, closes a gap in the school’s legal paperwork that had gone unresolved for decades, the outlet reported.

With the title secured, the institute can now seek federal and state funding to build new classrooms, expand its facilities and improve its infrastructure, according to the institute’s director, Benito Sánchez Raya.

Ramón Jiménez López, director general of the Tecnológico Nacional de México, recognized the mayor’s support in resolving the matter, according to the report.

The city also pointed to municipal education programs backing Tecnológico students and teachers, totaling 758,800 pesos, including support for 91 students through two programs in 2025 and a teacher-support program this year, plus free mobile internet access for students.

Federal Deputy Carlos Canturosas Villarreal, local Deputy Ana Laura Huerta Valdovinos and Notaries College president Oscar Mario Hinojosa Ramírez attended the ceremony, according to the report.

Sources: Nexus Tamaulipas, Nov. 18, 2026; Noreste Digital, Nov. 18, 2026.
